name: Gilt market
summary: Gilt yields near multi-decade highs ahead of a likely 5 Nov rate rise
state: The 10-year gilt yield was 5.29% at the 30 Oct close, near multi-decade highs; markets reopen on 2 Nov. A rise in Bank Rate from 3.75% to 4% is widely expected on 5 Nov after CPI inflation rose to 3.5% in September (HomeOwners Alliance, 28 Oct).
for_you: Fixed-rate mortgage and loan pricing follows gilt and swap rates, so new deals stay expensive.

sources.title: HomeOwners Alliance — Will the Bank of England raise interest rates on 5 November?
Cambridge Currencies — Bank of England base rate: next decision 5 November

why: Gilt yields set UK mortgage rates and the government's borrowing costs; the 2022 LDI crisis showed how fast it can break.
drivers: Fiscal credibility, BoE policy, inflation, global bond moves, pension-fund flows.

rubric.alert: BoE intervention, or 10y moved > 75bp in a month.
rubric.watch: 30y gilt at multi-decade highs, or 10y moved 40–75bp in a month, or a weak auction.
rubric.normal: 10y gilt moved < 40bp in a month and auctions orderly.
